title: Identifying Linear Dynamics from Three Gaussian Snapshots with Unknown Common Measurement Noise
banked_reason: Banked downgraded on 2026-09-09 during Lean formalization: the derivation had passed review at field tier, but the cold D0.5.G re-score under the projected-paper-score rule gave 7.4 and tier subfield, and the run was banked on that tier; the run did not fail and is a re-raise candidate.
tldr: Three independent Gaussian snapshots have an exact dimension-dependent identification frontier under one unknown common positive-definite measurement covariance.  When \(p=2\) and \(d_0\ne0\), the two raw \(O(1)\) completions have opposite determinants and the negative-determinant completion fails the principal-logarithm cut, so model-compatible laws identify the full explanation.  The exceptional \(d_0=0\) regime retains a continuous \(O(2)\) ambiguity.  For \(p\ge3\), three snapshots generically retain a continuous \(O(p-1)\) ambiguity, whereas a fourth snapshot generically identifies through \(K_1K_0^{-1}\).  The four-snapshot block Gram certificate enumerates the raw stabilizer fiber; stability, the logarithm cut, Stein reconstruction, and strict noise positivity then determine exact structural compatibility.  Stabilizer dimension equals information nullity, and the sharp finite-fiber maximum is \(2^{p-1}\).  On each specified regular finite branch, a fixed-ball global residual projection is uniquely selected near the population moment and supports Gaussian moment inference, although a data-based global initializer and stable labeling rule across all noncyclic branches remain open.
gap: Published snapshot-identification theorems either assume known propagated noise or treat the observed covariance as the latent covariance. They do not classify the compatible generator and shared unknown measurement-covariance fiber, and existing numerical methods do not certify all branches.
fill: The paper supplies an if-and-only-if block Gram certificate, a bijective admissibility map, a sharp three-versus-four snapshot frontier, complete exceptional and exponential-fiber results, rational perturbation theory, branchwise inference, and a concrete \(\alpha\)-certification handle for the remaining global empirical-labeling problem.
